personSeniorities.title: Seniority Levels

package.name: gtm
package.packageFile:
$schema: ../_schema/package.schema.json

# Two vendors, one package: Apollo.io for company and people data, Hunter.io for email.
# One credential each, one base URL each, no SDKs.
#
# The retired TypeScript is at `_legacy/nodes/gtm/`.

name: gtm
displayName: Go To Market
description: Company and people discovery, enrichment and email verification
version: 2.0.0
category: productivity
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1775374180/gravity/icons/apollo.jpg

features:
  - Apollo company and people search, with filters
  - Apollo company and people enrichment
  - Hunter email discovery, finding and verification

allowedHosts:
  - api.apollo.io
  - api.hunter.io

requires:
  credential: [apiKeyHeader, apiKeyQuery]
  transport: [json]
  paginate: [page]
  executorVersion: ">=1.4.0"

credentials.apolloCredential.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

name: apolloCredential
displayName: Apollo.io
description: Apollo.io master API key for people and organisation search
documentationUrl: https://docs.apollo.io/docs/create-api-key

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Apollo.io master API key, required for the search endpoints
    placeholder: ""
credentials.hunterCredential.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

name: hunterCredential
displayName: Hunter.io
description: Hunter.io API key for email discovery, verification and enrichment
documentationUrl: https://hunter.io/api-documentation/v2

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your Hunter.io API key, found under API in your Hunter dashboard
    placeholder: ""

shared.apollo.yaml:
# What every Apollo call shares.
#
# The key travels in the `x-api-key` HEADER, which is `apiKeyHeader`, an executor
# capability. `Cache-Control: no-cache` is sent because the retired client sent it: Apollo
# is documented as caching search responses, and dropping the header would silently change
# which results come back.

credential: &credential
  scheme: apiKeyHeader
  header: x-api-key
  value: "{{ credentials.apolloCredential.apiKey }}"

headers: &headers
  Cache-Control: no-cache

# NOTE for the bodies below: every filter is a comma-separated config field turned into the
# array Apollo wants, with
#
#   String(config.x || '').split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean)
#
# and an EMPTY array is left out of the body rather than sent, because Apollo reads an empty
# filter as "match nothing" rather than as "no filter". That is why each body is built by an
# expression that assembles only the keys that have values, instead of a static object.
shared.hunter.yaml:
# What every Hunter call shares.
#
# TWO auth styles, and that is Hunter's doing rather than ours: `/discover` takes the key in
# an X-API-KEY header, every other endpoint takes it as an `api_key` query parameter. Both
# are executor capabilities, so each call names the one its endpoint wants.

queryCredential: &queryCredential
  scheme: apiKeyQuery
  param: api_key
  value: "{{ credentials.hunterCredential.apiKey }}"

headerCredential: &headerCredential
  scheme: apiKeyHeader
  header: X-API-KEY
  value: "{{ credentials.hunterCredential.apiKey }}"

# Hunter wraps every payload in `data` and reports failures in `errors`, sometimes with a
# 200. Without this a quota error would emit an empty result and read as "not found".
error: &error
  when: "return !!(response.errors && response.errors.length)"
  message: "return response.errors.map(e => e.details || e.id).join('; ')"

# A LinkedIn URL to the handle Hunter wants. split/join rather than a regex, because the
# expression sandbox takes no regex literal: everything after /in/, up to a ? or #, with any
# trailing slash removed.
linkedinHandle: &linkedinHandle >-
  return String(config.linkedinHandle || '').trim()
    .split('/in/').slice(-1)[0]
    .split('?')[0].split('#')[0]
    .split('/').filter(Boolean).slice(-1)[0] || ''

files.api/events.yaml:
# One row per output connector, in interface.yaml order.
#
# `last_name` falls back to `last_name_obfuscated`: Apollo hides the surname on records your
# plan has not unlocked, and dropping it would leave the name looking truncated rather than
# redacted.

- emit: people
  from: response
  value: >-
    return (response.people || []).map(p => ({
      id: p.id || "",
      name: p.name || ((p.first_name || "") + " " + (p.last_name || p.last_name_obfuscated || "")).trim(),
      first_name: p.first_name || "",
      last_name: p.last_name || p.last_name_obfuscated || "",
      title: p.title || "",
      email: p.email,
      linkedin_url: p.linkedin_url,
      twitter_url: p.twitter_url,
      github_url: p.github_url,
      facebook_url: p.facebook_url,
      city: p.city,
      state: p.state,
      country: p.country,
      departments: p.departments,
      seniority: p.seniority,
      headline: p.headline,
      photo_url: p.photo_url,
      phone_numbers: p.phone_numbers,
      organization: p.organization ? {
        id: p.organization.id || "",
        name: p.organization.name || "",
        website_url: p.organization.website_url,
        linkedin_url: p.organization.linkedin_url,
        twitter_url: p.organization.twitter_url,
        facebook_url: p.organization.facebook_url,
        primary_domain: p.organization.primary_domain,
        logo_url: p.organization.logo_url,
        industry: p.organization.industry,
        estimated_num_employees: p.organization.estimated_num_employees,
        city: p.organization.city,
        state: p.organization.state,
        country: p.organization.country,
        short_description: p.organization.short_description
      } : undefined
    }))

# The distinct organisations behind those people, first occurrence wins.
- emit: organizations
  from: response
  value: >-
    return (response.people || [])
      .map(p => p.organization)
      .filter(Boolean)
      .filter((o, i, all) => !!o.id && all.findIndex(x => x.id === o.id) === i)

- emit: totalCount
  from: response
  value: "return (response.pagination || {}).total_entries || 0"

- emit: page
  from: response
  value: "return Math.round(config.page || 1)"

- emit: perPage
  from: response
  value: "return Math.round(config.perPage || 25)"
files.api/run.yaml:
# ONE page, not a walk. This node takes `page` as a config field, so the caller chooses
# which page; ApolloCompany walks pages because it takes a total instead. Two nodes, two
# deliberately different contracts, and the retired code did the same.
#
# Note the key names: domains go in as `q_organization_domains_list` here, and as
# `organization_domains` in the company search. Apollo's own asymmetry, kept verbatim.

- name: search
  method: POST
  url: https://api.apollo.io/api/v1/mixed_people/api_search
  credential: { $ref: apollo#credential }
  headers: { $ref: apollo#headers }
  body: >-
    return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries({
      per_page: Math.round(config.perPage || 25),
      page: Math.round(config.page || 1),
      person_titles:
        String(config.personTitles || '').split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean),
      organization_names:
        String(config.organizationNames || '').split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean),
      q_organization_domains_list:
        String(config.organizationDomains || '').split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean),
      person_locations:
        String(config.personLocations || '').split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean),
      person_seniorities:
        String(config.personSeniorities || '').split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean),
      person_departments:
        String(config.personDepartments || '').split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean)
    }).filter(e => !Array.isArray(e[1]) || e[1].length > 0))
  transport: json
  retry:
    attempts: 3
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]
files.config.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/config.schema.json

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: []
  properties:
    personTitles:
      type: string
      title: Person Titles
      description: Comma-separated job titles, e.g. 'CEO, CTO, VP Engineering'
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    organizationNames:
      type: string
      title: Organisation Names
      description: Comma-separated company names, e.g. 'Google, Meta'
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    organizationDomains:
      type: string
      title: Organisation Domains
      description: Comma-separated company domains, e.g. 'google.com, meta.com'
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    personLocations:
      type: string
      title: Person Locations
      description: Comma-separated locations, e.g. 'New York, London'
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    personSeniorities:
      type: string
      title: Seniority Levels
      description: Comma-separated seniorities, e.g. 'senior, manager, director, vp, c_suite'
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    personDepartments:
      type: string
      title: Departments
      description: Comma-separated departments, e.g. 'engineering, sales, marketing'
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    perPage:
      type: number
      title: Results Per Page
      default: 25
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 100
    page:
      type: number
      title: Page
      description: Which page to fetch. Apollo allows 500 pages, 50,000 records.
      default: 1
      minimum: 1
      maximum: 500

    # WHO MAY RUN THIS BOX, set by whoever builds the workflow (15-who-can-run-it.md).
    #
    # INSTANCE config, not the manifest's `auth`, and the two answer different questions.
    # The manifest is the node author's FLOOR: "this node is inherently privileged". These
    # are the builder's, per box on the canvas, because the same node type legitimately
    # faces staff on one workflow and customers on another.
    #
    # A role especially has to live here: `finance:approve` is a claim THIS deployment's
    # identity provider mints, and a node published to the marketplace cannot know the role
    # vocabulary of every universe that installs it.
    #
    # The executor takes the STRICTER of the two. Neither can loosen the other.
    authRequired:
      type: boolean
      title: Require sign-in
      description: Only signed-in callers can run this step.
      default: false
      "ui:widget": toggle
    authRole:
      type: string
      title: Require role
      description: A claim the caller must carry, like finance:approve.
      default: ""
      "ui:dependencies": { authRequired: true }

"ui:order":
  [authRequired, authRole, personTitles, personSeniorities, personDepartments, personLocations, organizationNames, organizationDomains, perPage, page]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/interface.schema.json

inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    description: Trigger. Filters may template from upstream output.

outputs:
  - name: people
    type: array
    description: Matched people with their profile and organisation
  - name: organizations
    type: array
    description: The distinct organisations those people belong to
  - name: totalCount
    type: number
    description: Total matching records in Apollo, which normally exceeds one page
  - name: page
    type: number
    description: The page returned
  - name: perPage
    type: number
    description: Page size used

credentials:
  - name: apolloCredential
    required: true
    displayName: Apollo.io
files.node.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/node.schema.json

type: ApolloPeople
kind: PromiseNode
name: Apollo People
category: Go To Market
color: "#F5D800"
description: Search Apollo.io for people by title, seniority, department or company
whenToUse: >
  Pick to DISCOVER lists of people by title, seniority, department or company filters,
  returning each with email, LinkedIn and phone in one call. Use it to find unknown people
  by role across companies; enriching one already-known person, or finding companies, are
  different jobs.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  cacheable: true

# One vendor. The package allows Hunter too, for its other five nodes.
allowedHosts: [api.apollo.io]
files.test.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/test.schema.json

testData:
  config:
    personTitles: CTO
    organizationNames: ""
    organizationDomains: ""
    personLocations: ""
    personSeniorities: ""
    personDepartments: ""
    perPage: 5
    page: 1
  inputs:
    signal: {}
  expect:
    people: "return output.people.length > 0 && typeof output.people[0].title === 'string'"
    organizations: "return Array.isArray(output.organizations)"
    perPage: "return output.perPage === 5"
